plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Under Section 3 of the Companies Act, 2013, what is the minimum number of persons required to form a public company?
options: Two persons
Seven persons
Three persons
Ten persons
plain.explanation: Section 3 of the Companies Act, 2013 stipulates that a public company may be formed for any lawful purpose by seven or more persons. For a private company, the requirement is two or more persons, and for an OPC, only one person is needed.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Incorporation of Company and Matters Incidental Thereto

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which of the following documents contains the fundamental conditions upon which a company is allowed to be built under the Companies Act, 2013?
options: Articles of Association
Memorandum of Association
Prospectus
Certificate of Incorporation
plain.explanation: The Memorandum of Association (MoA) is the charter of the company and defines its scope of operations, objects, and the limits outside which a company cannot act. It forms the foundation upon which the company is built.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Incorporation of Company and Matters Incidental Thereto

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: A One Person Company (OPC) must nominate a nominee in its memorandum. When is the prior written consent of such nominee required to be filed with the Registrar?
options: At the time of incorporation
Within 30 days of incorporation
At the time of filing annual return
Within 60 days of incorporation
plain.explanation: Rule 3 of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014 mandates that the memorandum of an OPC shall indicate the name of the nominee who shall, in the event of the subscriber's death or incapacity, become the member. The prior written consent of this nominee must be filed with the Registrar at the time of incorporation.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: What is the maximum permissible period within which a newly incorporated company must maintain its registered office from the date of incorporation under Section 12?
options: 15 days
30 days
45 days
60 days
plain.explanation: Section 12(1) of the Companies Act, 2013 requires a company to have a registered office capable of receiving and acknowledging all communications and notices within 30 days of its incorporation.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Incorporation of Company and Matters Incidental Thereto

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Under Section 7(4) of the Companies Act, 2013, for how many years must a company preserve all books and papers relating to its incorporation at its registered office?
options: 3 years
5 years
8 years
From the date of incorporation till its dissolution
plain.explanation: Section 7(4) of the Companies Act, 2013 mandates that the company shall maintain and keep at its registered office copies of all documents and information originally filed with the Registrar until its dissolution.

Central Government (Registrar of Companies)
Securities and Exchange Board of India
Regional Director
plain.explanation: Under Section 13 read with the relevant rules, a change of name of a company requires a special resolution and approval of the Central Government (delegated to the Registrar of Companies).

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Incorporation of Company and Matters Incidental Thereto

options: 10 days
20 days
30 days
60 days
plain.explanation: As per Rule 9 of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014, the Registrar shall reserve a name for a new company for a period of 20 days from the date of approval (or such extended period as may be permitted upon payment of additional fees).

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Incorporation of Company and Matters Incidental Thereto

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: What is the consequence if a company is found to have been incorporated by furnishing false or incorrect information or by suppressing any material fact under Section 7(7)?
options: Only a compounding fine on the promoters
The Tribunal may direct winding up, or direct that liability shall be unlimited
Automatic conversion into a partnership firm
Mandatory imprisonment of all independent directors
plain.explanation: Section 7(7) empowers the Tribunal (NCLT), on an application made to it, to pass orders such as directing the regulation of the management, winding up of the company, or declaring that the liability of the members shall be unlimited, when incorporation has been obtained by fraud or false information.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Incorporation of Company and Matters Incidental Thereto

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Can a charitable company registered under Section 8 alter the objects clause in its Memorandum of Association?
options: Yes, by ordinary resolution and Central Government approval
Yes, by special resolution and prior approval of the Central Government
No, Section 8 companies can never alter their objects
Yes, simply by filing an e-form with the ROC without any special resolution
plain.explanation: Under Section 8(4)(i), a Section 8 company cannot alter the provisions of its memorandum or articles except with the previous approval of the Central Government, and such alteration must also comply with provisions regarding special resolutions.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Incorporation of Company and Matters Incidental Thereto

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a permissible form of pre-incorporation contract liability ratification by a company under Indian company law?
options: Express novation of contract
Adoption of the contract by the company after incorporation
Automatic statutory ratification upon obtaining the Certificate of Incorporation
Entering into a new contract on the same terms after incorporation
plain.explanation: Pre-incorporation contracts cannot be ratified automatically upon incorporation because a company does not exist prior to its incorporation. Valid legal options include novation, fresh contract, or specific adoption as per Indian Contract Act principles.

90 days
180 days
365 days
plain.explanation: Rule 3(7) of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules specifies that where a person is a member in one OPC and becomes a nominee in another such company, such person shall meet the eligibility criteria within a period of 180 days.

options: Name clause
Registered office state clause
First directors appointment clause
Liability clause
plain.explanation: Section 4 lists the mandatory clauses of the Memorandum: Name, State, Objects, Liability, and Capital. The appointment of first directors is typically dealt with in the Articles or separate board resolutions/regulatory filings, not as a mandatory clause of the MoA.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Incorporation of Company and Matters Incidental Thereto

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Under Section 10 of the Companies Act, 2013, what is the legal effect of the registered Memorandum and Articles of Association once they are bound?
options: They bind the company and its members as if signed by each member
They are merely recommendatory guidelines
They are binding only on the promoters
They have no legal standing until a court order is passed
plain.explanation: Section 10 states that when the memorandum and articles are registered, they bind the company and the members thereof to the same extent as if they respectively had been signed by each member and contained covenants on the part of each member to observe all provisions.

Private company
Banking company
Non-banking financial company registered with RBI
plain.explanation: While public companies can accept deposits under strict regulations, private companies are generally restricted from accepting deposits from the general public (though they can accept from members/directors as per exemptions). However, looking strictly at the chapter on incorporation and basic rules, private companies cannot invite deposits from the public.

30 days
60 days
90 days

Board Resolution only
Unanimous Resolution

National Company Law Tribunal (Central Government)
Securities and Exchange Board of India
High Court

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Can a minor be a subscriber to the Memorandum of Association of a company under the Companies Act, 2013?
options: Yes, through a natural guardian
No, a minor's agreement is void ab initio, hence a minor cannot be a subscriber
Yes, provided the share capital is fully paid up
Yes, if approved by the Board of Directors
plain.explanation: Since a minor lacks the capacity to contract under the Indian Contract Act, 1872, a minor cannot be a subscriber to the memorandum of association. Shares cannot be allotted to a minor except if they are fully paid and acquired by way of transfer/transmission.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: What is the status of the doctrine of indoor management in relation to the Memorandum and Articles of Association?
options: It protects the company from outsiders
It protects outsiders dealing with the company from internal irregularities
It allows directors to bypass the Articles
It overrides statutory provisions of the Companies Act
plain.explanation: The doctrine of indoor management (Turquand's Rule) protects outsiders who deal with a company in good faith from being affected by internal irregularities or procedural non-compliance within the company.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Incorporation of Company and Matters Incidental Thereto

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Under Section 3A of the Companies Act, 2013, if the number of members of a public company falls below seven and it continues to carry on business for more than how many months, every such member shall be severally liable?
options: 3 months
6 months
9 months
12 months
plain.explanation: Section 3A provides that if the number of members is reduced below the statutory minimum (7 for public, 2 for private) and business is carried on for more than 6 months, every person who is a member during that time with knowledge shall be severally liable for the payment of debts contracted during that time.

plain.prompt: Which of the following cannot be included in the name of a company unless previous approval of the Central Government is obtained?
options: Industrial
Cooperative
Federal
Limited
plain.explanation: Rule 8 of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules specifies words which require prior approval of the Central Government, such as 'Federal', 'Republic', 'State', 'Bank', 'Union', etc., as they might imply government patronage.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Incorporation of Company and Matters Incidental Thereto

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: What does the 'Doctrine of Ultra Vires' signify in company law?
options: Acts done by directors beyond their authority but within company powers
Acts done beyond the powers of the company as defined in its Memorandum
Acts done by members without board approval
Internal management procedures
plain.explanation: An act is ultra vires the company if it is beyond the powers conferred upon the company by its Memorandum of Association. Such acts are void and cannot be ratified even by all members.

Yes, if it has a local agent
No, but it has 180 days to register

It creates a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal (optional)
It makes directors personally liable for all future debts
It requires annual renewal of incorporation
plain.explanation: Section 9 provides that from the date of incorporation, the subscribers to the memorandum and other persons shall be a body corporate capable of exercising all functions, having perpetual succession and a common seal.

options: Immediately upon getting the Certificate of Incorporation
Only after filing a declaration under Section 10A regarding receipt of subscription money
After holding its first Annual General Meeting
After obtaining a separate trading license from the High Court
plain.explanation: Section 10A of the Companies Act, 2013 stipulates that a company having a share capital cannot commence any business or exercise borrowing powers unless a director files a verification declaration within 180 days that every subscriber has paid the value of shares agreed.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: If a promoter makes a secret profit from a transaction entered into on behalf of a prospective company, what is the legal remedy available to the company?
options: The company can only reprimand the promoter
The company can rescind the contract and recover the secret profit
The company must pay an additional bonus to the promoter
The contract becomes automatically binding with no remedies
plain.explanation: Promoters stand in a fiduciary position towards the company they promote. They cannot make any secret profits, and if they do, the company can compel them to account for such profits or rescind the contract.

Audited balance sheet of promoters for the last 3 years
Declaration by professionals and subscribers in INC-9

scenarios.subject: Law
scenarios.passage: Mr. Rohan, an enthusiastic entrepreneur, decides to start a software development business in Pune. He plans to register a private limited company named 'TechInnovate Solutions Private Limited' with five initial subscribers. He prepares the Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association. During the incorporation process, Rohan acts quickly to secure a commercial property as the registered office, but due to delays in final paperwork, the registered office address is registered 45 days after the date of incorporation.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Incorporation of Company and Matters Incidental Thereto

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Is the registration of the registered office address within 45 days compliant with Section 12 of the Companies Act, 2013?
options: Yes, because private companies get a grace period of 60 days
No, Section 12 requires the company to have a registered office within 30 days of incorporation
Yes, if approved by the Regional Director
No, but it attracts only a minor fee without legal consequences
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 12(1) of the Companies Act, 2013 mandates that a company must have a registered office capable of receiving communications within 30 days of its incorporation. Registering it after 45 days is a non-compliance.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: With five subscribers, does 'TechInnovate Solutions Private Limited' satisfy the minimum subscriber requirement for a private company?
options: No, a private company requires at least seven subscribers
Yes, a private company requires a minimum of two subscribers, and five is compliant
No, it must have exactly ten subscribers
Yes, but only if all subscribers are corporate bodies
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Section 3 of the Companies Act, 2013, a private company requires a minimum of two persons to form it. Having five subscribers fully satisfies this legal requirement.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the legal nature of the Memorandum and Articles prepared by Rohan once the company is successfully incorporated?
options: They are bilateral agreements between Rohan and the Registrar
They constitute a contract between the company and its members as per Section 10
They are internal guidelines that do not bind the members
They have no legal force until approved by NCLT
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Section 10, once registered, the MoA and AoA bind the company and its members to the same extent as if they had been signed by each member, establishing a statutory contract.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: If Rohan had instead decided to form a One Person Company (OPC) for the same business, what would have been the mandatory requirement regarding a nominee?
options: No nominee is required for software businesses
A nominee must be appointed whose prior written consent is filed with the Registrar at incorporation
A nominee must be a public financial institution
The nominee must hold 51% of the shares
linkedMcqs.explanation: For an OPC, Rule 3 requires the memorandum to indicate the name of a nominee who shall become the member in case of death or incapacity, and their prior written consent must be filed at incorporation.

scenarios.subject: Law
scenarios.passage: A group of six philanthropic individuals intend to incorporate a company under Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013, named 'GreenEarth Foundation', with the object of promoting environmental awareness and wildlife conservation. They intend to apply all their profits towards promoting their objects and prohibit the payment of any dividend to their members. They submit their application for a license to the Central Government / Registrar.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Incorporation of Company and Matters Incidental Thereto

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Is 'GreenEarth Foundation' eligible for a Section 8 license with six initial subscribers?
options: No, Section 8 requires a minimum of 50 subscribers
Yes, Section 8 companies can be formed by individuals or associations for charitable objects without any special high subscriber minimums beyond standard private/public rules
No, charitable companies must be registered as public companies with at least 7 subscribers
Yes, but they must have a minimum capital of 50 lakhs
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 8 allows persons or associations of persons to form a company for charitable objects with restricted profit distribution. They can be registered as private or public companies complying with basic member requirements.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Can 'GreenEarth Foundation' alter the objects clause in its Memorandum of Association after incorporation?
options: No, Section 8 company objects can never be altered
Yes, but only with the previous approval of the Central Government and via special resolution
Yes, by passing a simple board resolution
Yes, by notifying the local municipal authority
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 8(4) stipulates that a Section 8 company cannot alter the provisions of its memorandum or articles except with the previous approval of the Central Government.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: What happens to the restriction on payment of dividends for members of 'GreenEarth Foundation'?
options: Dividends can be paid up to 10% per annum
Dividends are strictly prohibited, and profits must be applied solely to the promotion of its objects
Dividends can be distributed if approved by ordinary resolution
Dividends are permitted only after 5 years of operation
linkedMcqs.explanation: A Section 8 company is prohibited from paying any dividend to its members; its profits and income must be applied solely for the promotion of the objects for which it is established.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: If at any time the Central Government revokes the Section 8 license of 'GreenEarth Foundation' due to violation of conditions, what action can the Government take?
options: Only impose a monetary penalty on the founders
Direct the company to wind up or amalgamate with another Section 8 company having similar objects
Automatically convert the company into an unlimited partnership
Dissolve the company and forfeit all its assets to the promoters
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Section 8(6), upon revocation of the license, the Central Government may order the company to be wound up, or amalgamated with another Section 8 company, after giving an opportunity of being heard.

scenarios.subject: Law
scenarios.passage: Apex Infrastructure Limited is an existing public company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013. The Board of Directors wishes to alter the Articles of Association to include restrictive clauses on share transfers and wants to convert the company into Apex Infrastructure Private Limited. The company has 80 members on its register. The management calls an extraordinary general meeting to pass the necessary resolutions.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Incorporation of Company and Matters Incidental Thereto

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: What type of resolution is required for altering the Articles of Association under Section 14 of the Companies Act, 2013?
options: Ordinary Resolution
Special Resolution
Unanimous Board Resolution
Resolution requiring 100% consent
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 14 of the Companies Act, 2013 explicitly states that a company may alter its articles by passing a special resolution.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: To convert Apex Infrastructure Limited into a private company, whose approval is mandatory under the Companies Act, 2013?
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
Central Government (Regional Director / Tribunal)
Reserve Bank of India
Registrar of Companies only via e-form without sanction
linkedMcqs.explanation: Conversion of a public company into a private company requires the sanction/approval of the Central Government (powers delegated to Regional Director/Tribunal) in accordance with Section 13 and 18 read with rules.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Does the number of members (80 members) comply with the maximum limit prescribed for a private company under the Companies Act, 2013?
options: No, the maximum limit for a private company is 50 members
Yes, the maximum limit for a private company is 200 members
No, private companies cannot have more than 20 members
Yes, because public companies converting to private have no member limits
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 2(68) defines a private company as one which has a minimum of 2 members and restricts the maximum number of its members to 200 (excluding employee-members and past employee-members). 80 members is well within this limit.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: If a dissenting minority shareholder challenges the conversion in court, what is the primary consideration the Tribunal evaluates?
options: Whether the conversion prejudices the interests of shareholders or creditors
Whether the company has paid dividends for the last 10 years
Whether the company's registered office is in a metropolitan city
Whether the promoters are Indian citizens
linkedMcqs.explanation: When evaluating conversion of a public company to a private company, the Tribunal/Central Government ensures that adequate provision is made for safeguarding the interests of creditors and dissenting shareholders.

scenarios.subject: Law
scenarios.passage: Mr. Vikram starts a trading business and promotes 'Vikram Agro-Products Private Limited'. During the promoter stage, before obtaining the Certificate of Incorporation, Vikram enters into a lease agreement on behalf of the prospective company with a landlord for a warehouse. After the company is incorporated, the board of directors continues to use the warehouse and pays rent, but never formally executes a new contract or novates the old agreement.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Incorporation of Company and Matters Incidental Thereto

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the legal status of the lease agreement entered into by Vikram prior to incorporation?
options: It is automatically binding on the company from day one
It is a pre-incorporation contract which is not automatically binding on the company unless adopted/novated
It is completely illegal and void under criminal law
It binds the landlord personally with no recourse
linkedMcqs.explanation: Pre-incorporation contracts entered into by promoters on behalf of a yet-to-be-formed company are not automatically binding on the company upon incorporation unless the company adopts the contract or enters into a fresh novation.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Can the company adopt or ratify the pre-incorporation contract expressly after its incorporation?
options: Yes, by adopting it or entering into a new contract on the same terms (novation)
No, a company can never adopt a pre-incorporation contract under any circumstance
Yes, automatically after 6 months of use
Only if approved by the National Company Law Tribunal
linkedMcqs.explanation: While ratification in the strict agency sense is not possible because the principal (company) did not exist when the contract was made, the company can become bound by entering into a new contract (novation) or specific adoption.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: What position do Vikram and the other promoters hold in relation to the prospective company during the promotion phase?
options: They are mere employees with no fiduciary duties
They stand in a fiduciary relationship towards the company
They are statutory directors automatically
They act as legal guardians of the company
linkedMcqs.explanation: Promoters stand in a fiduciary (position of trust) relationship with the company they promote, meaning they must not make secret profits and must act in good faith.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: If Vikram had made a secret profit from the lease transaction without disclosing it to the subscribers, what remedy is available to the company?
options: The company can recover the secret profit or rescind the transaction
The company must reward Vikram with additional shares
The contract becomes voidable only at the option of the landlord
No remedy, as promoters are immune from profits
linkedMcqs.explanation: If a promoter makes a secret profit in a transaction on behalf of the company, the company can compel the promoter to disgorge the secret profit or rescind the transaction for breach of fiduciary duty.

scenarios.subject: Law
scenarios.passage: Zenith Global Limited is incorporated with an authorized share capital of 50 lakhs divided into equity shares. The Certificate of Incorporation is issued by the Registrar of Companies on 1st October. The directors are eager to commence business operations and issue a large supply order on 10th October without filing the statutory declaration required under Section 10A of the Companies Act, 2013.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Incorporation of Company and Matters Incidental Thereto

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Is Zenith Global Limited legally permitted to commence business operations or exercise borrowing powers on 10th October?
options: Yes, because incorporation gives immediate commencement rights
No, a company having share capital cannot commence business without filing the Section 10A declaration regarding subscription money
Yes, if the board passes an ordinary resolution
No, unless approved by SEBI
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 10A explicitly prohibits a company having a share capital from commencing business or exercising borrowing powers unless a director files a declaration verifying that every subscriber has paid the value of shares.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Within what maximum time frame from the date of incorporation must the Section 10A declaration be filed by a director?
options: 30 days
60 days
180 days
365 days
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 10A(1)(a) requires that the declaration by a director must be filed with the Registrar within a period of 180 days of the date of incorporation of the company.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: What are the penal consequences for the company and defaulting officers if business is commenced in violation of Section 10A?
options: Only a warning letter from the ROC
Penalty of fifty thousand rupees for the company and one thousand rupees per day for defaulting officers, plus potential removal of name
Immediate imprisonment of all shareholders for 7 years
Mandatory dissolution by High Court order only
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 10A prescribes a penalty of fifty thousand rupees for the company and one thousand rupees for each day during which the default continues for every officer in default, along with Registrar action for striking off if no business is commenced.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: From which date does Zenith Global Limited acquire its corporate personality and perpetual succession?
options: From the date of filing the SPICe+ form
From the date mentioned in the Certificate of Incorporation
From the date of the first board meeting
From the date Section 10A declaration is filed
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Section 9, from the date of incorporation mentioned in the Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar, the subscribers become a body corporate with perpetual succession.
